note: Written through the gateway by GET /api/eval?task=dialogue; beats checked word for word.

lines.text: Hello, hello. Can people hear me okay?
Yep, I can hear you. You're a bit quiet though, maybe it's just me.
Let me, hold on, I'll move the microphone closer. Is that better?
Better, yeah. Much better.
Morning, everyone. Sorry, am I frozen? My picture's doing the thing where it just stops.
You were frozen for a second, now you're moving. Mid-sentence, actually, you had your mouth open.
Great, so that's my look for the day. I'll turn my camera off and on again, one moment.
Classic. Switch it off and on. Works for everything.
Okay, back. Can you see me properly now?
Yes, crisp and clear. Hi, Ahmad.
Hi Lisa. Hi Tom. I think we're all here, that's four of us.
Sorry, I've got a slight echo on my side. Let me mute the other tab, I think the old meeting is still open somewhere.
Yes, I can hear myself a little bit, a half-second late. Is that you, Tom?
Probably. Hang on. Okay, found it, closed it. Is it gone?
Gone. Lovely.
Did everyone get through the week all right? It felt very long to me.
It did. It's one of those weeks where Monday feels like a month ago.
Mm-hm. And it's gone dark so early now, I looked up at four o'clock and thought it was night.
Same here. I had the lamp on all afternoon.
I keep making coffee later and later in the day to cope. Not a good plan.
That's exactly my plan, so I can't say anything.
Right, well, I've got mine here, so I'm ready.
Okay, shall we start? I'll share my screen in a second, it's just the sprint board, nothing fancy. Can you see it?
Not yet. Just a grey box with your name.
Ah. Let me stop and share again. There. Now?
Yes, there it is. A bit small but I can read it.
Same, it's readable.
Good. Right, thanks for joining everybody. We'll go through the sprint goal, the demo, the billing API, the pen test and the release cut-line.
Sounds good.
Sprint two goal was e-mail sign-up and viewing bills. Ahmad, demo please.
Okay. Let me share my screen as well, give me a moment, I need to stop yours, sorry Mei.
Go ahead, I've stopped. You should be able to share now.
Right, can you see the test site? The sign-up page with the portal logo on top?
Yes, I see it.
I see it too. The logo's a bit blurry but that's probably the video.
Probably the video, yes. So, I'll go through the sign-up now. I'm typing in an e-mail address, choosing a password, and pressing the button at the bottom.
Mm-hm.
And then it takes me to the page that says check your inbox. And, here, I'll switch to the mailbox, the confirmation e-mail has just landed.
That was quick.
Yes, it's usually a few seconds on the test site. And I click the link in it, and I'm in, I'm signed in to the portal.
Sign-up with e-mail is done and working on the test site, including the confirmation e-mail.
Good. So that half of the goal is finished, as far as the board goes.
As far as I'm concerned, yes. It's been through everything I could think of to try.
Does the confirmation e-mail look the same in different mail programs? Or have you only tried the one?
I tried it in a couple. It looked fine in what I tried. I wouldn't promise it's perfect everywhere, though.
No, that's fair. I was just asking.
Can you go back to the page after the sign-up, the one with the empty bills area?
Sure, here. This is the account page. And this box here, this is where the bills would show.
And it's empty right now.
It's empty, yes. Viewing the last twelve bills is not done, it's blocked on the billing system API.
Right. So there's nothing to show there at all, not even fake data?
I could put in placeholder rows to make it look nice, but it wouldn't prove anything. It'd just be me pretending, really.
No, no, I wasn't asking you to. I just wanted to be clear what we're looking at.
Understood. What you see is what's there.
Can I go back to the sign-up part? I tried it myself on the test site yesterday, before this call.
Yes, please. Go ahead.
The sign-up flow looks good, but the error message for a used e-mail is confusing, can we reword it?
Which one is that? Do you mean when you type an address that's already registered?
Yes, that one. I typed one that already had an account, and it gave me a message that I had to read twice to understand.
Can you show us what it says, Ahmad? I haven't seen it.
Sure, let me type one in. Here, it comes up in red, under the e-mail box.
Oh. Yes. I see what Lisa means. It sounds more like something went wrong with the system than with the address.
Right, that's it. A normal person would think the site is broken.
Mm-hm. It's a fair point, a customer would just get stuck there.
Yeah, I wrote that one quickly, to be honest. It was a placeholder in my head and then I never went back to it.
It happens. I'm not saying it's bad, just that it could say it more plainly.
Yes, small fix, I'll add it to the next sprint.
Okay. I'll make sure it's noted down with the demo feedback.
Sorry, just checking, so is the sign-up counted as finished for this sprint, with the wording being separate?
I'd say so, yes. The sign-up works, the wording is a tidy-up. Ahmad, you agree?
I agree. It works, it's just the sentence that needs changing.
I'm fine with that. I didn't want to make it sound bigger than it is.
No, no, it's a good catch. Better now than after customers see it.
Right. Anything else on the demo before we move on? Anyone?
Only that the page loaded fast. I was expecting it to be slower on the test site.
Ha, thanks. I'll take that.
Nothing from me. Oh, wait, sorry, one thing. The e-mail link, when you clicked it, did it open in the same window?
It opened a new tab, and then signed me in there. So the old one stays behind.
Okay. That's what I thought I saw. Just wanted to check I wasn't imagining it.
Okay. Let's talk about the billing API since it's blocking.
Yes. Do you want me to start, Mei?
Please. You've been talking to them, haven't you?
I have, a bit. It's mostly through messages, and one call. So, the billing team says the API is ready on the eighteenth of December, but their last two dates slipped.
Sorry, the last two? So this is the third date we've been given?
That's how I count it, yes. Two earlier ones that didn't happen, and now this one.
Did they say why the earlier ones slipped? Because if I knew what's holding them up, I'd feel a bit more comfortable with the new one.
Not in any detail. They just said it wasn't ready. I didn't want to push too hard on the call.
Mm. Okay. That's the bit that worries me, honestly. A date without a reason is just a date.
Well, we do have a date. Let's not make it sound like we have nothing.
No, I know, I'm not saying it's nothing. I'm just saying I'd trust it more with a reason.
I'd say it both ways. It's good that they gave us a date, but I understand Ahmad being a bit careful, after two misses.
Yes, that's fair. I'm not very confident either, if I'm honest. I'm just reporting what they told me.
Okay. And Ahmad, just so we're clear on your side, you can't do anything on the bills until you've got the API?
Not really, no. I can't see the real bills without it. I can build the screen around nothing, but I can't check it works.
Right. So the bills story can't finish until the billing team delivers the API.
That's it exactly. Yes.
Mm-hm.
And I should add something about what depends on it. And if it slips again past the holidays, paying a bill by card moves out of the first release.
Wait, say that again? Paying by card is what moves out, not just the bills view?
Paying a bill by card, yes. That's what I said. The bills view is the part that's already waiting.
Okay, I just wanted to be sure I heard it right. That's a bigger deal than I'd thought.
It does make sense, though. You can't pay a bill you can't see.
True. When you put it like that, it's obvious. It's just a bit sad to hear it out loud.
Tom, when you say past the holidays, you mean if the eighteenth doesn't hold?
That's how I understood it. If the date slips again, and it goes past the holidays, then the card payment can't be in the first release.
Okay. I just wanted to hear it in your words.
So is anybody comfortable with the eighteenth? Just a quick feel.
I'd say, hopeful. Not comfortable.
Hopeful is about right. I'd say the same.
I'd say the same as well. But that is what we've been given, so that's what we're working with for now.
Yes. Yes, fine. I just wanted us to say it out loud so nobody's surprised later.
Fair enough. Nobody's pretending.
Can I check one more thing? The eighteenth, that's when the API is ready on their side, and not when we have bills showing in the portal?
Right, that's their date for the API. It's not our date for the screen.
Okay, good, thank you. I mixed those up for a second.
Easy to do. I did too when I first read it.
Okay. Is there anything else on the billing API, or can I move on?
Nothing else from me. I've said everything I know.
No, I'm fine.
Nothing. Go on.
Okay. Security test booking.
That one's mine. So, security wants a penetration test before go-live and the testing firm needs three weeks' notice.
Three weeks. So it's not something you can just ring up and get for next Tuesday.
No. It's not like that at all.
Is it a must, though? Before go-live? Or is it more of a nice-to-have?
Security's position is that they want it before go-live. I wouldn't call that optional.
Okay. I only asked because I didn't know.
No, it's a reasonable question. I'd rather you ask than guess.
Lisa, do the three weeks start when we ask them, or when the money's agreed, or something? I don't know how these things work.
It's three weeks' notice, that's what they told us. I'm not going to guess beyond that.
Fine. That's good enough for me.
What do they actually test? Is it the whole portal, or just the sign-up part?
I don't have the details of that. I only know they want a penetration test, and what the notice is.
Okay. No problem. I was just curious.
And we're assuming the test can run in the second half of January with no major findings.
Hang on. The no major findings part. Is that something we're assuming, or something we know?
Assuming. That's why I said it that way. It's what the plan is built on.
Right. Okay. I just want to make sure we all hear that word, assuming.
Mm-hm. Because if there are major findings, that's a different conversation.
Yes. I'm not saying there will be. I'm saying that's what we're assuming.
Understood. I think we all heard it. We're planning on the basis that there aren't any.
Yep. That's all I wanted.
And second half of January. So that's after the holidays.
Yes, it's after. That's what I said, second half of January.
Okay, yes, I just wanted to put it in my head next to the billing date.
Same, I was putting those two side by side as well.
Right. And the testing firm, they've not got a slot held for us yet, as far as I can tell?
Not that I know of, no. That's why I raised it.
Lisa, can you book the slot this week so we have it?
Will do.
Thanks, Lisa.
Yes, thank you. That's one less thing to hang over us.
Right. Let me just look at the clock. We're about halfway, so that's about where I'd hoped we'd be.
Good. We've done well.
Okay, let me close that board and pull up the next thing. Give me a second.
Release cut-line. We said we'd decide this today.
Right, we did. We kept pushing it back and I think everyone's a bit tired of it hanging over us.
Yeah, I'd like to get it settled. Can I just check what we're actually choosing between? Because I've got it a bit muddled in my head.
Sure. Good question. Basically it's what goes in the first release and what waits.
Okay. So it's not about whether those pieces get built at all, it's about which release they land in.
Exactly. It's about the cut-line, where we draw it.
Mm-hm. And the billing API is the thing that's driving it, isn't it? That's what we were talking about before the break.
Yeah, that's the one. The billing API sits underneath a lot of what we'd show.
Sorry, when you say underneath, you mean the bills screen and the payment part both lean on it?
Both of them touch it, yes. I'd say payment touches it more, but I'm thinking aloud, I wouldn't want to put a number on how much more.
Fair. I wouldn't either.
Okay, let me just put something on the table so we've got a concrete thing to react to.
Given the billing API, I propose release one is sign-in, viewing bills and service requests, and card payment goes to release two.
Right. So sign-in, viewing bills, service requests. Those three are in.
Those three, yes.
And card payment is the only thing that moves.
That's the only thing that moves, as I'm proposing it.
Can I ask something? When you say viewing bills, that's just looking, right? Not paying them.
Right, just viewing. Customers can see their bills, they can't pay them by card in release one.
Okay. I just wanted to hear it said out loud so we're all picturing the same thing.
Yeah, that's helpful, because in my head I was sort of half picturing the pay button greyed out, and that's not what we're saying.
No, I'm not saying greyed out. I'm saying it's a release two item.
Okay, okay. Fine. Good to be clear.
Mm. I do keep coming back to it, though. Paying is kind of the thing people want from a portal, isn't it?
I mean, that's a fair point. It's a big one.
I'm not saying no. I'm just saying it's the obvious thing people would look for.
No, that's fair, and I'm not going to pretend it isn't. That's why I wanted us to talk about it rather than just announce it.
Yeah. And that's where my head is too, actually.
Go on, Tom.
Well, I was going to say, the other side of it is what happens if we hold everything for payment.
Right, so we'd be waiting.
We'd be waiting, and then nothing goes out. Whereas the other three things are, you know, they stand on their own.
They do stand on their own, I'd agree with that. Sign-in doesn't need payment. Service requests don't need payment.
And viewing bills doesn't either, you said.
Viewing bills is on the billing API, but it's not the payment piece. That's how I understand it, anyway.
That's how I understand it too.
Okay. I was just checking I hadn't misheard.
No, no, you didn't.
Does anyone want to push back on the proposal? Ahmad, you've gone a bit quiet.
Sorry, no, I'm just, I'm turning it over. I don't have a strong objection. I think I just wanted to make sure it was a real choice and not, you know, a done deal.
It's a real choice. We've said we'd decide today, so I'd rather hear it if anyone disagrees.
Okay. Then no, I don't disagree. It makes sense to me.
I'm kind of in the same place. I'd say I lean towards it, but I want to hear Tom, because he's the one who'll have to explain it.
Ha, yeah, thanks for that.
Sorry. But it's true.
No, it's true. It's fine.
Finance won't love it, but I'd rather ship on time.
Mm-hm. Right.
Yeah. I think that's honest.
I appreciate you saying that plainly, Tom.
Well, no point dressing it up. They'll have a view. I just think a release that's out is better than one that's late.
Is that something we need to talk through more, the Finance side? Or is it just, they'll be disappointed and that's that?
I mean, I'm not going to pretend I know exactly how they'll react. That's just my guess. I only meant they won't be thrilled.
Right, and that's all we've got on that. I don't want us to invent more than we know.
No, that's fine. I wasn't trying to open a can of worms. I just wanted to make sure it wasn't something we were skipping over.
I don't think we're skipping it. Tom's named it. It's a trade-off and we're saying it out loud.
Yeah, it's a trade-off. We're choosing the on-time one.
Okay. Then I'm fine with it.
Yeah, me too.
Just so I'm sure, let me go round. Lisa, you're fine with card payment going to release two.
I'm fine with it, yes.
Ahmad?
Fine. Yes.
Tom, obviously, you've said.
Yep. I'm in.
Okay, so decided: card payment moves to release two.
Good. That feels better, honestly. Having it open was bugging me.
Same. It's a relief to have a line drawn.
Mm. Yeah.
Can I just say the three things back one more time, so the notes are right? Sign-in, viewing bills, service requests in release one.
Yes. And card payment in release two.
Great. That's what I've got.
That's what I've got as well.
Same here. Nothing to add.
Good. Anything else on the cut-line before we leave it? Anyone feel it's not quite closed?
Not from me.
No, I think we're good.
I'm good. It's a decision, let's leave it as one.
Ha, yes. Let's not reopen it next time.
Please, no. Okay.
Last thing, January capacity.
Right, that one. I know it's about who's around, but I haven't seen the detail. Ahmad, is that yours?
Yeah, that's me. I've been looking at the people side of it.
Is this the leave thing? I vaguely remember something about it.
It is, yes. Let me just make sure I say it properly.
Two of our four developers have leave in the first week of January, so velocity will be about half that sprint.
Okay. So two out of four. That's half the developers.
Half the developers, so about half the velocity. That's the rough maths.
Sorry, just checking, because I want to be sure I follow. Is it half of the sprint, or half of the team for the sprint?
Half the team. The sprint is the sprint, it's the same length. It's that we have half the people for that first week.
Okay, right. And velocity is about half. Not exactly half.
About half. I wouldn't say exactly. It's approximately, I'm not going to claim it's precise.
That's fair. Two over four is half, so about half sounds right.
Yes. It's the simple version of it.
Is the leave definitely booked? Or is it, like, they might take it?
I've got it as leave they have in that week. That's what I've been told, and that's all I'm going on.
Okay. That's good enough for me. I just wanted to hear it.
Mm. It does sound like it's, you know, settled.
It sounds settled to me, yeah.
And it's the first week of January. Not the whole month.
The first week. That's what I've said. That's the sprint where it hits.
Right, and the other sprints aren't part of this conversation.
Not that I'm raising now, no.
Okay. I think I've got it. Half the developers, about half the velocity, that one sprint.
That's it. That's the whole thing.
I suppose the question is, is that a problem? Or is it just a fact we need to hold in our heads when we plan?
I'd say it's the second. It's a thing we know.
Yeah, it's not like someone's leaving or it's a surprise. It's leave.
It's normal. People take leave.
No, totally. I wasn't trying to make it sound like a drama. I just wanted to be sure we weren't brushing past something.
No, I think that's right to ask. And my read is, it's fine.
That's fine, it's planned leave, we'll plan the sprint smaller.
Okay. Good. That's how I'd have gone at it too.
Mm-hm. Makes sense.
Smaller sprint, half the people. It adds up.
It does. It's nice when the maths is that tidy.
Ha, it doesn't happen often.
No, it really doesn't.
Can I loop back to something from earlier, just quickly? On the cut-line. I want to be sure I've got the release one list right in my head, since we've now talked about capacity.
Sure.
Sign-in, viewing bills, service requests. Release one. Card payment, release two.
Yes, that's right.
Okay. I'm not linking the two topics, I just wanted to hold them both clearly.
No, that's sensible. They're separate. One's about scope, one's about people.
Right. Scope and people.
Yes. I don't want us to blur them either. We decided the cut-line, and separately we know about January.
Agreed.
Yeah, agreed. I'd keep them apart.
Fine by me.
Anything else on January? Any questions on the leave, or the half velocity?
I don't think so. I think it's clear.
No, nothing from me. I've said what I know.
Nothing. I'm happy.
Okay. Then I think that's us. That was the last topic.
Good, and we've still got a few minutes, which is a nice change.
Ha. Don't say that out loud.
Right, quick wrap-up. We settled the release cut-line, with card payment moving to release two. And we've noted the January capacity, and we'll plan that sprint smaller.
Yep, that's both of them.
That's how I've got it too.
Same. Good meeting.
Thanks, everyone. Good discussion today, and thanks for being straight about the trade-off.
Thanks, Mei. Thanks, all.
Thanks. Bye, everyone.
Bye, all. Cheers.
Bye, everyone.
